description: Educational prompt content catalog for Demo_Educational_Triggers. Three-tier structure (intro/detail/advanced) with context filters for time-of-day, weather, and player progress.
derived_from: Written by domain expert (geologist). Shareable hooks designed for stream visibility and Steam trailer moments.

sedimentary_intro.text: This canyon wall tells an ancient story. The layered sandstone you see was once an ancient seabed, compressed over 300 million years into stone.

sedimentary_crossbedding.text: Look at the angled lines in the rock -- that's cross-bedding. Ancient sand dunes migrated across this landscape, and their windward slopes were frozen in stone when the dunes were buried.

sedimentary_dunes.text: The ripple marks preserved in this sandstone are fossilized wind patterns. Each ridge tells us the prevailing wind direction 200 million years ago. The wind that shaped this stone never stops -- it just changes what it sculpts.

sedimentary_fossils.text: Fossil fragments in the limestone -- tiny marine organisms that lived in a shallow sea that covered this land. Their calcium carbonate shells became the rock beneath your feet.

sedimentary_overlook.text: Look back at the canyon entrance. Those red and orange bands are different sedimentary layers, each representing a different geological era. You are walking through 500 million years of history.

transition_sed_to_meta.text: Notice the rock changing. The sedimentary layers are giving way to metamorphic rock. Heat and pressure deep in the Earth's crust transformed soft sandstone into hard schist.

metamorphic_folding.text: This red rock was once flat layers of sediment, folded like dough by immense tectonic pressure. The folds you see happened deep underground over millions of years. Erosion revealed them.

metamorphic_foliation.text: The vertical bands in this schist are foliation -- minerals aligned by pressure. Think of it as rock memory: when the Earth squeezes, the minerals line up like books on a shelf. These bands record an ancient mountain-building event.

erosion_water.text: This gully was carved by water. Even in a dry canyon, flash floods sculpt the rock. Notice how the softer schist layers erode faster than the harder quartz veins -- differential erosion at work.

tectonic_fault.text: A fault line runs through here. The rock layers on one side have shifted vertically relative to the other. This planet's crust is alive -- slowly moving, always changing.

confluence_geology.text: Two canyons meet here, and their rock stories are different. Each branch carved through different geological layers. The confluence is where those stories converge.

metamorphic_overlook.text: From here you can see the folded strata stretching across the canyon wall. Each fold is a chapter in the planet's tectonic history. This is what 100 million years of compression looks like.

igneous_granite_intro.text: This massive granite formation was once a chamber of molten magma, cooling slowly deep underground. The large crystal grains tell us it cooled over millions of years. Erosion stripped away the rock above and exposed it.

igneous_basalt_columns.text: Hexagonal columns in basalt -- one of nature's most geometric formations. When lava cools, it contracts and cracks into perfect hexagonal shapes. The same pattern forms in drying mud and cooling glass.

igneous_lava_flow.text: This dark rock is a lava flow bed. The ropey texture is 'pahoehoe' -- smooth, ropy lava that flowed like slow-moving taffy. When the surface cooled and crusted over, the molten interior kept moving, wrinkling the surface.

igneous_fossil_contact.text: Here, molten magma baked the surrounding sedimentary rock, creating a metamorphic halo. The heat was intense enough to recrystallize the minerals. This contact zone is a frozen moment of geological violence.

igneous_crystals.text: Crystal-lined cavity -- a geode. Hot mineral-rich water seeped into a gas bubble in the cooling magma, and over thousands of years, crystals grew inward. Each crystal face is a record of the chemical soup it grew in.

terminus_summary.text: The full canyon in view. You started at sedimentary rocks at the entrance, walked through metamorphic in the middle, and ended at igneous -- the three great rock classes in a single walk. This canyon is a geology textbook written in stone.

weather_wind_erosion.text: Wind erosion shapes everything here. The wind picks up sand and uses it like sandpaper against the rock. That's why the softer layers wear away faster, creating these hoodoo formations.

weather_storm_approach.text: Pressure dropping fast -- a storm is building. In a canyon, flash floods are the real danger. The same water that carved these walls can fill them in minutes.

astronomy_night_sky.text: Without atmospheric distortion, the stars are razor-sharp. Each pinprick of light is a sun, many with their own worlds. The dark band across the sky is our galaxy's core -- 100,000 light-years of stars.

tier_advancement.rule: On each revisit to the same zone_id, advance: not_seen -> intro -> detail -> advanced -> advanced (repeat). Player progress per zone_id tracked in save data.
tier_advancement.fallback: If a tier has no prompt for current context (time/weather mismatch), try next lower tier before skipping.

required_time.description: If set, prompt only fires during this time-of-day. null means any time.

required_weather.description: If set, prompt only fires when weather system matches. null means any weather.

suppression_tags.description: Prompts are suppressed while player has these GameplayTags. Prompt queues and fires on exit.

test_mode.description: When 1, forces sequential fire of all prompts at player location, 3s apart, logging each to output log.
